title: Data Analysis
blurb: Ask sharp questions, clean data, use statistics correctly, and turn analysis into decisions with clear charts and stories.

quiz.question: Delivery times are right-skewed. Which summary best describes the typical customer experience?
quiz.explanation: The median is robust to the long tail; add p90 to describe bad experiences.

quiz.question: What does a p-value of 0.03 mean?
options: 3% chance the null hypothesis is true
If there were no real effect, data this extreme would occur about 3% of the time
quiz.explanation: A p-value is computed assuming the null is true; it is not the probability the null is true.

quiz.question: Why is stopping an A/B test as soon as p < 0.05 a problem?
options: Repeated peeking inflates the false-positive rate
It makes the test underpowered for guardrails only
It is fine if the lift is large
quiz.explanation: Checking repeatedly gives many chances to cross the threshold by chance; fix the duration or use sequential methods.

quiz.question: A 50/50 experiment ends with 52.5%/47.5% of 200,000 users. What should you suspect?
options: Sample ratio mismatch from an assignment or logging bug
quiz.explanation: Such an imbalance at that scale is extremely unlikely by chance; results cannot be trusted until fixed.

quiz.question: Revenue is summed from UTC timestamps for a Dhaka business. What can go wrong?
options: Orders near midnight land on the wrong day/month
quiz.explanation: Asia/Dhaka is UTC+6, so late-evening orders shift dates; convert to the business time zone first.

quiz.question: Which chart is best to show change in a metric over 12 months?
quiz.explanation: Line charts show trends over time; bars compare categories.

problems.title: Explain a metric drop
problems.prompt: Repeat orders fell 12% in September. Describe your investigation.
problems.solution: Verify the data (freshness, definitions, time zones, logging changes), segment by city, platform, cohort and channel to localise, line up changes (releases, pricing, competition, seasonality), quantify contributions, and recommend actions with confidence levels.

problems.title: Design an A/B test
problems.prompt: Plan a test of a new checkout flow.
problems.solution: State the hypothesis and one primary metric (conversion), guardrails (refunds, latency), run a power analysis for the minimum detectable effect, randomise by user, run whole weeks without peeking, check sample ratio, analyse the effect with CI, correct for multiple metrics, document the decision.
